The '''2022 Islington London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. All 51 members of [[Islington London Borough Council]] were to be elected. The elections took place alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]].

In the [[2018 Islington London Borough Council election|previous election in 2018]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] maintained its control of the council, winning 47 out of the 48 seats with the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] providing the only opposition councillor, [[Caroline Russell]]. The 2022 election took place under new election boundaries, with an increase in the number of councillors to 51.

== Background ==

=== History ===
[[File:Islington London UK local election 2014 map.svg|thumb|Result of the 2018 borough election]]
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Islington has been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control, [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control, [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrat]] control, [[Social Democratic Party (UK)|Social Democratic Party]] control and [[no overall control]]. Labour most recently gained control of the council in the [[2010 Islington London Borough Council election|2010 election]], winning 35 seats to the Liberal Democrats' 13 seats. The Liberal Democrats lost all their remaining seats in the [[2014 Islington London Borough Council election|2014 election]], with Labour winning 47 and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]]'s [[Caroline Russell]] winning a single seat in Highbury East. In the [[2018 Islington London Borough Council election|most recent election in 2018]], Labour held their 47 seats with 60.6% of the vote across the borough while Russell held her seat for the Green Party, with the Greens winning 16.4% of the vote across the borough. The Liberal Democrats won 12.3% of the vote and the Conservatives won 9.7% of the vote, but neither won any seats.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Grove|first=Tristan|date=2018-05-04|title=Islington elections 2018: Labour wins biggest share of vote since 1974|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/local-council/islington-elections-2018-labour-wins-biggest-share-of-vote-since-3794098|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref>

=== Council term ===

A Labour councillor for St George's ward, Kat Fletcher, resigned in November 2019. A by-election to replace her was held on 12 December 2019, coinciding with the [[2019 United Kingdom general election|2019 general election]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cumiskey|first=Lucas|date=2019-11-01|title=Labour councillor resigns prompting December 12 by-election in St George's ward|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/st-george-s-ward-set-for-december-12-by-election-3828386|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> The Labour candidate Gulcin Ozdemir, who worked as a social housing advocate, successfully defended the seat, with the Green Party candidate coming in second place.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gelder|first=Sam|date=2019-12-13|title=Labour's Gulcin Ozdemir wins Islington Council by-election for St George's ward|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/local-council/labour-s-gulcin-ozdemir-wins-islington-council-by-election-for-3830462|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref>

Gary Poole, a Labour councillor, left his party to sit as an [[independent politician|independent]] in July 2019 citing [[antisemitism in the Labour Party|antisemitism]], saying he hoped to rejoin in the future.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cumiskey|first=Lucas|date=2019-07-15|title=Islington councillor Gary Poole, who has quit Labour: 'Jeremy Corbyn's ideological beliefs providing safe space for antisemitism'|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/islington-councillor-gary-poole-resigns-from-labour-party-over-alleged-3819464|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> In October 2020, the Labour councillor Rakhia Ismail left her party, saying she had faced racism in the party.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-11|title=Former Islington mayor quits Labour party over racism|url=http://www.theguardian.com/politics/2020/oct/11/former-islington-mayor-quits-labour-party-over-racism|access-date=2021-10-19|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref> She joined the Conservative Party in November 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-11-10|title=Exclusive: Ex-Labour mayor defects to Tories over Sadiq Khan's record on crime|url=https://www.cityam.com/exclusive-ex-labour-mayor-defects-to-tories-over-sadiq-khans-record-on-crime/|access-date=2021-10-19|website=CityAM|language=en-GB}}</ref> A Labour councillor for Hollway ward, Paul Smith, resigned in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bartholomew|first=Emma|date=2021-01-12|title=Holloway by-election planned as Cllr Paul Smith stands down|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/holloway-by-election-planned-as-paul-smith-resigns-6892976|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref>

A Labour councillor for Bunhill, [[Claudia Webbe]], was elected as MP for [[Leicester East (UK Parliament constituency)|Leicester East]] in the 2019 general election. She resigned as a councillor in March 2021 as a by-election to replace her was not possible until May 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bartholomew|first=Emma|date=2021-03-23|title=Claudia Webbe's resignation triggers Bunhill by-election|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/bunhill-by-election-set-to-go-ahead-7837666|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> In March 2021, three Labour councillors announced their resignations: Andy Hull of Highbury West ward because his family were moving to Morocco; Joe Calouri of Mildmay ward because of work and family commitments; and Vivien Cutler of St Peter's ward.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bartholomew|first=Emma|date=2021-03-26|title=By-elections set for Highbury West, Mildmay and St Peter's wards|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/three-more-by-elections-announced-7855040|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref> By-elections for all five seats were held on 6 May 2021 alongside the [[2021 London mayoral election]] and [[2021 London Assembly election|London Assembly election]].<ref name="five">{{Cite web|last=Fraser|first=Calum|date=2021-04-16|title=Get ready! Islington set for five ballot box battles for seats on the same day|url=http://islingtontribune.com/article/get-ready-islington-set-for-five-ballot-box-battles-for-seats-on-the-same-day|url-status=live|website=Islington Tribune|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420071000/http://islingtontribune.com/article/get-ready-islington-set-for-five-ballot-box-battles-for-seats-on-the-same-day |archive-date=20 April 2021 }}</ref> Some of the elections were contested by independent candidates opposed to [[Low Traffic Neighbourhood|low traffic neighbourhoods]].<ref name="five" /> Labour held all five seats: Valerie Bossman-Quarshie won Bunhill, Bashir Ibrahim won Highbury West, Jason Jackson won Holloway, Angelo Weekes won Mildmay and Toby North won St Peter's.<ref>{{Cite web|title=By-election results announced for Bunhill, Highbury West, Holloway, Mildmay and St Peter's wards|url=https://www.islington.media/news/by-election-results|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Council News|language=en-GB}}</ref> The Green Party came second in three wards and the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats came second in one ward each.<ref>{{Cite web|last=reporter|first=Ed Sheridan, Local democracy|date=2021-05-07|title=Winners of Islington by-elections speak|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/local-council/election-2021-islington-by-elections-results-7957158|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref>

Richard Watts stood down as council leader and leader of the Labour group in 2021, and [[Kaya Comer-Schwartz]] was chosen unopposed to take over. Comer-Schwartz had served as deputy leader of the council since 2020 and had previously worked for a mental health charity.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bartholomew|first=Emma|date=2021-03-26|title=Kaya Comer-Schwartz set to be Islington Council's new leader|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/kaya-comer-schwartz-to-be-new-council-leader-7855258|access-date=2021-10-19|website=Islington Gazette|language=en-UK}}</ref>

As with most London boroughs, Islington will be electing its councillors under new boundaries decided by the [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]], which it produced after a period of consultation. The number of councillors will rise to 51, an increase from the previous 48, across seventeen three-councillor wards.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LGBCE {{!}} Hounslow {{!}} LGBCE Site|url=http://www.lgbce.org.uk/all-reviews/greater-london/greater-london/hounslow|access-date=2021-10-19|website=www.lgbce.org.uk|language=en}}</ref>

== Campaign ==
In March 2022, groups of residents supportive and opposed to [[Low Traffic Neighbourhood]] schemes protested Islington Town Hall ahead of a debate triggered by an anti-low traffic neighbourhood petition. One attendee, the driving instructor David Corringall, cited the schemes as the reason he was standing as a Conservative candidate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=Julia Gregory Local Democracy |date=2022-03-07 |title=Islington consulted on future of low traffic neighbourhoods |url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/pro-and-anti-ltn-protests-islington-town-hall-8739300 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=Islington Gazette |language=en-UK}}</ref>

== Electoral process ==
Islington, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. This election used [[plurality block voting]], with each ward being represented by three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there were councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who lived at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work |url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=London Councils}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />
